assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy is a rare complete arc from hormone discovery and peptide characterization to drugs that have changed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with growing evidence for cardiovascular and renal benefit. The impact on clinical practice and physiology is large, lasting and unambiguous.
assessment.attribution: Holst established the physiology of GLP-1 and its incretin action, Drucker defined its biology, intestinotropic actions and therapeutic rationale, and Mojsov identified the bioactive GLP-1(7-36) form. Knudsen led development of long-acting analogues and is a strong alternative, so the fourth credited name makes a three-person limit difficult; I choose the discovery and mechanism core.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed in multiple large outcome trials and in routine use for years; recognition is timely and arguably urgent.
uncertainties: Allocation between discovery scientists and the industrial drug developer (Knudsen) is the main unresolved question.
Priority for GLP-1(7-36) identification involved several groups, and I rely on my own recollection of that history rather than verified sources.
Long-term safety and durability of the therapeutic effect are still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells as a living therapy produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new therapeutic modality. The concept, receptor engineering and clinical proof are all of high originality and impact.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain led the design and clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T cells with costimulatory domains, and Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and gene-engineered lymphocytes in patients. Early chimeric receptor concepts from other investigators (not credited here) such as Eshhar complicate a clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and more than a decade of follow-up show durable responses; limitations in solid tumours remain, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric antigen receptor concept versus the clinical translation is disputed and some pioneers are absent from the supplied names.
Toxicity (cytokine release, neurotoxicity, secondary malignancy) and access remain limits on the therapeutic story.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new intracellular signalling logic in which the endoplasmic reticulum communicates folding stress to the nucleus. It is conceptually original, clean and broadly relevant to secretory biology, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently defined the IRE1-HAC1/XBP1 signalling pathway and its mechanism, including unconventional splicing. The two-person attribution is natural and compact.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of confirmation across yeast and mammals, with therapeutic modulators now in development; timing is ripe. The medical link is more indirect than for some other candidates.
uncertainties: Translational impact is still emerging, which may weigh against it in a Physiology or Medicine context.
Contributions from others who identified IRE1 and ATF6 or PERK arms are not in the supplied names, and I have not verified their relative weight.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with millisecond precision, and has transformed circuit analysis across model organisms. As a neurologist I recognize its methodological impact, though clinical translation is limited so far, mainly in retinal restoration.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) discovered and characterized channelrhodopsin as a light-gated channel, and Deisseroth established its use in mammalian neurons and behaviour. Boyden, Miesenböck and Bamberg have strong claims, and six credited names exceed the three-laureate limit, which makes this a hard allocation.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and used for two decades; timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Several equally strong claimants exist and the choice of three is contested.
Credit for first demonstration in neurons (Boyden/Deisseroth versus Zemelman/Miesenböck) is disputed.
Therapeutic application is still early.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR identified a central regulator linking nutrient and growth-factor signals to cell growth, with relevance to cancer, immunosuppression, ageing and metabolism. Originality and downstream influence are very high.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR in yeast and established its role in growth control, and Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin and the mammalian target is foundational. Sabatini's contributions on mTORC1 regulation by amino acids are major but I would not include him given the uncertainty around his standing, which I cannot verify here; Sabatini is the alternative if the committee judged otherwise.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed and clinically embedded through rapalogs; mature.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hall, Schreiber, Sabatini and other early rapamycin and TOR investigators is unresolved.
Therapeutic benefit of rapalogs is narrower than the biology would suggest.
I have not verified contested non-scientific information about one credited person.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defined how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity, with implications for infection, autoimmunity (interferonopathies), cancer immunotherapy and ageing. This is a clear mechanistic discovery of broad impact.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide 2'3'-cGAMP as the second messenger, and Barber discovered STING; both are decisive. Co-credited trainees (Sun, Wu, Ishikawa) contributed but a prize would more likely recognize the two principal investigators.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly confirmed, but therapeutic agents are still in trials and the field is still expanding, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Therapeutic validation in patients is limited.
The relationship of Barber's STING work to parallel discoveries (Ishikawa, others) needs care.
Prize timing could favour waiting for clinical maturity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and the validation of BCR-ABL as a drug target turned chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal disease into a manageable one and established the template for targeted cancer therapy. Clinical impact is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the discovery of the inhibitor, Druker drove clinical development and proof of concept, and Sawyers showed resistance mechanisms and developed second-generation inhibitors. Rowley and Nowell and others on the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL gene fusion are not in the supplied names, which makes this a downstream-only recognition.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of follow-up and robust confirmation; recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: The upstream cytogenetic and oncogene discoveries are not covered by these names, so the prize might look incomplete.
Industrial and academic roles are intertwined, and my recollection of precise contributions is unverified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) produced the first effective disease-modifying treatment for spinal muscular atrophy, with a striking effect on a severe childhood neuromuscular disease. As a neurologist I see the clinical impact as dramatic, and it validated splice-modulating antisense therapeutics broadly.
assessment.attribution: Krainer identified the splicing mechanism and the target sequence, and Bennett led development of the antisense chemistry and drug. The pairing is clean and fits a two-person allocation.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term follow-up; the mechanism is confirmed. Recognition is timely, though the field of oligonucleotide therapeutics is still maturing.
uncertainties: Contributions of Adrian Krainer's collaborators (for example Hua, Singh) and earlier SMN gene discovery by Melki and Lefebvre are not in the supplied names.
Limits of efficacy in later-treated patients and the role of competing SMA therapies (gene replacement, risdiplam) may affect how the discovery is framed.
